reference_title: Drilled Shafts: Construction Procedures and LRFD Design Methods
chapter_title: Appendix A: Design Example: Drilled Shafts for Replacement Bridge

sections.title: General
sections.body: Design example: drilled shafts for a replacement bridge, based on an actual project; the owner is a state transportation agency and the site is in the Atlantic Coastal Plain physiographic province. It illustrates the LRFD procedures of the manual and draws on Chapter 2 (site characterization), 8 (design process), 9 (lateral loading), 10 (axial loading) and 12 (structural design) (p. A-1). The example follows Figure 8-1 'Drilled Shaft Design and Construction Process', assuming Steps 1 through 6 complete and a decision to evaluate drilled shafts (Step 7); Step 11 (axial) is presented before Step 10 (lateral) because axial load controls the final dimensions. The bridge is a 6-span structure, 1,230 ft long and 57 ft wide, on two abutments (driven pile groups) and five piers on drilled shafts; spans 175 to 220 ft; AASHTO Modified Type VI spliced post-tensioned girders; the trial design calls for three 8-ft diameter drilled shafts per pier, each supporting an 8-ft diameter pier column, with a cast-in-place pier cap; the shaft-column joint is 1 ft above mean high water (MHW). Design is focused on Pier No. 2 (Figure A-1). Step 8, Define Subsurface Profile for Analysis: 32 borings plus 32 borings made in 1953 for the existing bridge; Pleistocene lowland alluvial deposits over Tertiary marine sediments, locally covered by recent tidal marsh soils (compressible organic silts and peat from mudline to depths of 10 to 30 ft); the alluvium is alternating or intermixed quartz sand and gravel with silt and clay lenses; the Tertiary deposits are medium to fine silty sands with localized clay layers and lenses (p. A-1). Figure A-2 shows the generalized subsurface profile and strata; the reference boring at Pier 2 is W-2, where strata R, C, D, E and F are present. Stratum R (river bed loose sand and organic soils, about 3.5 ft thick) is neglected, so the uppermost stratum is C, starting at elevation -29 ft. Field SPT N-values at Boring W-2 at 5 ft intervals are used to obtain soil properties for design (pp. A-2 to A-3).
key_points: Six-span, 1,230 ft bridge; three 8-ft diameter drilled shafts per pier; design focused on Pier 2 (p. A-1).
Step 11 (axial) is presented before Step 10 (lateral) because axial load controls the dimensions (p. A-1).
Reference boring W-2; stratum R neglected, top of stratum C at elevation -29 ft (p. A-2).
figures: Figure A-1: Pier Section of Proposed Bridge
sections.applicability: Worked LRFD design of 8-ft drilled shafts for a bridge pier in layered Coastal Plain soils with scour: axial (beta and alpha methods), lateral pushover and service deflection by p-y, and structural (P-M, shear) checks.

sections.title: Scour and Seismic Considerations
sections.body: The scour design flood gives total scour of 38 ft at Pier 2, to elevation -67 ft, removing the upper part of Stratum C; the full-scour profile is used for Strength I and Service I. Extreme Event I (earthquake): Seismic Performance Zone 1, but the owner designated the bridge essential and required site-specific response analyses; design parameters: peak ground acceleration, 1,000-year event, A = 0.052g; Site Class D (stiff soils); Seismic Importance Category essential; Seismic Performance Zone 1; elastic response coefficient Csm = 0.075. Extreme Event I does not include scour (owner specifications). The fill and sands at the piers are generally medium dense to dense and not subject to liquefaction (p. A-4). Step 9, Establish Limit States and Factored Drilled Shaft Load Demands: Strength I (with design-flood scour) for geotechnical axial compression, lateral geotechnical resistance and structural resistance of a single shaft; Extreme Event I for geotechnical axial compression; Service I (with scour) for settlement and horizontal movement at the top of the foundation (pp. A-4 to A-5). Demands came from finite element modeling of the bridge, shafts first modeled as 8.5-ft equivalent fixed-end columns (permanent casing from 2 ft below MHW to elevation -67 ft) from the joint to fixity 15 ft below mudline (10 ft below the scour line where scour applies), with nodes at mudline (elevation -29 ft) whose force effects are the shaft-top loads (Figure A-3). The iterative procedure: analyze the structure under factored loads (Tables 8-2 and 8-3) with assumed lateral springs; resolve the mudline force effects; analyze trial shafts by p-y; revise springs from the p-y stiffness profiles; re-analyze with shafts as beam-columns pinned at the depth of zero deflection; repeat until mudline deflections agree within +/- 20 percent; use the final demands for the LRFD checks (pp. A-5 to A-6). Table A-1 summarizes the factored demands at Pier 2 (p. A-6). Step 11, Establish Diameter and Depths for Axial Loads (Figure 10-2): 11.1 the profile at Pier 2 is divided into eight layers of cohesionless or cohesive soil (Figure A-4, Table A-2); with full scour Layer 1 and part of Layer 2 (to elevation -67 ft) are removed for Strength I and Service I; zero scour for Extreme Event I. 11.2 the shafts are designed for Strength I, Extreme Event I and Service I in axial compression (pp. A-6 to A-7). 11.3 cohesionless layers are analyzed drained (phi'), cohesive undrained (su); Table A-3 gives the friction angles of Layers 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7: each field N60 is corrected to (N1)60 by Eq. A-1 with pa = 2,116 psf and n = 0.5 for sandy soils, and where the coefficient of variation of a layer is within the limit (< 45%) its mean (N1)60 is correlated to phi' by Eq. A-2 (p. A-8). 11.4 trial diameter 8 ft and length 201 ft, mudline (elevation -67 ft) to tip (elevation -268 ft). 11.5 and 11.6 nominal and factored side and base resistances by spreadsheet (Table A-4): (A) Layer 3, beta method, Strength I with full scour: mean N60 = 30, mean sigma'v = 4,645 psf (no scour), 2,266 psf (full scour); mean (N1)60 = 21, phi' = 27.5 + 9.2 log(21) = 40 degrees, delta = phi = 40 degrees; sigma'p = pa [0.47 (N60)^m] = 2,116 psf [0.47 (30)^0.6] = 7,654 psf, OCR = 7,654 / 4,645 = 1.65; Ko = (1 - sin phi') OCR^sin phi' = 0.49 < Kp; beta = 0.49 tan 40 = 0.41; fSN = 0.41 (2,266 psf) = 936 psf; RSN = pi (8 ft)(20 ft) 932 lb/ft2 = 470,684 lb; resistance factor 0.55, factored 258,876 lb (pp. A-8 to A-10). (B) Layer 4, alpha method: mean UU su = 1,750 psf, CIUC equivalent by Eq. 10-17 su = 1,750 / 0.851 = 2,057 psf; alpha = 0.47; fSN = 976 psf; RSN = pi (8 ft)(15 ft) 967 lb/ft2 = 368,124 lb; resistance factor 0.45 (Table 10-5), factored 165,656 lb. (C) Base in Layer 7 (cohesionless): qBN = 0.60 N60 = 0.60 (41) = 24.6 tsf = 49.2 k/ft2 (N60 the average uncorrected field value over two diameters below the tip); RBN = pi/4 (8 ft)^2 49.2 k/ft2 = 2,473 kips; resistance factor 0.50, factored 1,236.5 kips. Sum of factored resistances 1,087,053 + 1,181,955 + 1,236,531 = 3,505,539 lb = 3,506 kips > 3,389 kips, so Strength I axial is satisfied (pp. A-10 to A-12). Extreme Event I (zero scour, all resistance factors 1.00): sum 9,932 kips > 2,823 kips (Table A-5). Service I: tolerable settlement 2.0 in; failure threshold RSN + RBN = (1,976.5 + 2,626.6) + 2,473.1 = 7,076.2 kips; normalized displacement 2 in / 96 in = 2.1%, which on Figure 10-40 (Figure A-5) gives 78%; test load 0.78 (7,076.2) = 5,519 kips; Rservice = 5,519 - 885.0 = 4,634 kips > 2,835.4 kips (pp. A-12 to A-14). Step 10, Establish Minimum Diameter and Depth for Lateral Loads (Figure 9-12): 10.1 the axial profile (Figure A-4, with p-y properties) is used, full scour of 38 ft for Strength I and Service I, none for Extreme Event I. 10.2 the 8-ft, 201-ft trial shaft is checked and minimum depths evaluated. 10.3 geotechnical strength by pushover analysis (Section 12.3.3.1): stable load-deflection behavior up to the maximum load multiple and deflection at the maximum load below 10% of the shaft diameter, the shaft modeled as a linear elastic uncracked beam (Table A-6). Strength I: resultant shear and moment with the minimum axial force 2,673.42 kips, top of pile 456 in above the ground surface, loads in multiples of 0.25 up to 1/phi = 1.5 times the factored values (phi = 0.67) (Table A-7); deflection reaches zero about 60 ft down (26 ft below the scour line); stable to 1.5 times with maximum deflection 1.06 in (Figures A-6, A-7); a 68-ft shaft (30 ft below scour) is still stable, a 62-ft shaft (24 ft) deflects 4 in at 1.5 times and shorter shafts do not converge. Extreme Event I: longitudinal demands with 30 percent of transverse (the critical case), minimum axial force 2,810.26 kips, no stickup, multiples of 0.25 up to 1.25 (phi = 0.80) (Table A-8); stable with maximum deflection 0.51 in; 30 ft is about the minimum length (27 ft exceeds 6 in at 1.25, 26 ft does not converge) (Figure A-8) (pp. A-14 to A-19). 10.4 preliminary flexure: MN (ft-k) = 27 D^3 = 13,824 ft-k for rho = 1% and 40 D^3 = 20,480 ft-k for rho = 1.5%, against Mmax = 40,981 in-k (Strength I) and 107,810 in-k (Extreme Event I), so 8-ft shafts suffice. 10.5 service: tolerable 1/2 in at the scour line; with 40 #14 bars, 6-in cover (rho about 1.25 percent), fc = 4,000 psi, fy = 60,000 psi and the minimum axial force 1,836.42 kips the deflection at 38 ft is 0.49 in (Figure A-9). 10.6 lateral loading alone needs about 65 ft; axial loading governs the length (pp. A-19 to A-21). Step 12, Finalize Structural Design of the Shafts and Connection to Structure (Chapter 12), for the 8-ft, 201-ft shafts with rho = 1.25 percent: 12.1 demands from Table A-1. 12.2 Pr = phi Pn = phi beta [0.85 fc' (Ag - As) + As fy] = 0.75(0.85)[0.85 x 4(7,238 - 90) + 90(60)] = 18,936.8 kips >> 3,389.5 kips (Equation 12-6). 12.3 p-y with nonlinear shaft properties gives moment and shear with depth (Figure A-10, Table A-9). 12.4 P-M interaction diagram (nominal crushing strength 29,703 kips), factored with phi = 0.75 for compression-controlled (strain up to 0.002) to 0.90 at extreme tension strain of 0.005 or more, interpolated between; Strength I points must lie within the factored curve and Extreme Event I (phi = 1.00) within the nominal curve; both do (Figure A-11). 12.5 shear: 425.6 kips (Extreme Event I) exceeds 0.5 phi Vc = 0.50 (0.90) 812.8 kips = 365.7 kips, so the code minimum transverse steel applies (Eq. 12-5): at s = 6 in, Av = 0.606 in2, No. 8 (Av = 0.785 in2); alpha = cos^-1 [6 in / (pi x 84 in)] = 88.7 degrees; Vn = Vc + Vs = 812.8 + 525.8 = 1,338.6 kips, check 0.25 fc' bv dv = 0.25 (4 ksi) 96 in (66.98 in) = 6,430 kips; Vr = 0.90 (1,338.6) = 1,204.7 kips > 158.2 kips (Strength I) and 425.6 kips (Extreme Event I). Minimum transverse steel extends to three diameters below the deepest moment fixity (110 ft below mudline + 24 ft = 134 ft), about 167 ft of shaft including the length above mudline to elevation +3.64 ft; No. 8 Grade 60 spiral at 6.0 in, reducible below (for example No. 5); clear spacings 5 in (hoops) and about 11 in (two-bar bundles), above the 5 in minimum of Chapter 6; below about 115 ft (zero moment) a ratio of 0.5 percent is acceptable, about 0.6 percent if one bar of each bundle stops. Connection: construction joint at elevation +5.0 ft (about 2.4 ft above M.H.W.), 40 #14 bars in bundles of two, mechanical couplers staggered, #8 hoops at 6 in continued 5 ft into the pier cap, permanent casing cut to 2 ft below M.L.W. (Figure A-12) (pp. A-21 to A-26). Step 13, Evaluate Constructability: alternating saturated coarse and fine layers, over-water construction, partial-length permanent casing and highly workable concrete; polymer drilling fluid with full slurry replacement before concrete where silt content was high; a crane-mounted rotary drill on a barge (Figure A-13), spoil barged to disposal; a tremie self-consolidating concrete mix (Section 7.6.1.2) for about 360 cubic yards a shaft placed over 8 to 10 hours, with high-range water reducer and retarder, high sand content and No. 8 crushed stone (1/2 in top size); slump flow 18 to 24 in; minimum 4,000 psi specified, 28-day breaks to 7,000 psi; Class F fly ash 20% of cementitious material, sand to total aggregate 0.48 (Table A-10, Figure A-14); no anomalies by cross-hole sonic logging (pp. A-26 to A-29).
key_points: Total scour 38 ft at Pier 2 (to elevation -67 ft) for Strength I and Service I; none for Extreme Event I (p. A-4).
PGA (1,000-year) A = 0.052g, Site Class D, Csm = 0.075 (p. A-4).
(N1)60 = N60 (pa/sigma'vo)^n with pa = 2,116 psf, n = 0.5 for sands (Eq. A-1); phi' = 27.5 + 9.2 log[(N1)60] (Eq. A-2) where the layer COV is under 45% (p. A-8).
Strength I axial: 3,389 kips < 3,506 kips; Extreme Event I 2,823 < 9,932 kips; Service I 2,835.4 < 4,634 kips (pp. A-11 to A-14).
Pushover: stable to 1.5 (Strength I) and 1.25 (Extreme Event I) times the factored loads, deflections 1.06 in and 0.51 in; minimum lengths about 62 to 68 ft and 30 ft (pp. A-16 to A-19).
Service lateral deflection 0.49 in at the scour line against 1/2 in, with rho about 1.25 percent (p. A-20).
Structural: Pr = 18,936.8 kips; Vr = 1,204.7 kips with No. 8 hoops at 6 in (pp. A-21 to A-24).
equations: Eq. A-1: (N1)60 = N60 (pa / σ'vo)^n; SPT N-value corrected for effective overburden stress (presented in Chapter 3), pa = atmospheric stress (2,116 psf), σ'vo = vertical effective stress at the depth of the SPT N-value measurement, n = 0.5 for sandy soils (p. A-8)

Eq. A-2: φ' = 27.5 + 9.2 log[(N1)60]; effective stress friction angle from the mean (N1)60 of a layer whose coefficient of variation is within the specified limit (≤ 45%) (presented in Chapter 3) (p. A-8)

sections.title: Summary
sections.body: An example design problem, based on an actual bridge project, is presented to illustrate the design procedures presented in this manual. Design of single drilled shafts for one of the piers (Pier 2) is illustrated for Strength I, Service I, and Extreme Event I limit states. Information obtained from the subsurface investigation is used to establish an idealized subsurface profile and to select soil properties used in the design equations. Design scour conditions are incorporated into the Strength I and Service I limit state analyses. Calculations are presented to illustrate limit state checks for geotechnical and structural resistances, for lateral and axial loading. Finally, constructability issues relevant to the project are identified and the measures taken to address them are discussed. (p. A-29)
key_points: Single shafts at Pier 2 checked for Strength I, Service I and Extreme Event I, with design scour in Strength I and Service I (p. A-29).
